tools.name: impact_get_framework
tools.description: Returns the IMPACT positioning method step by step: identify champions, map alternatives, pinpoint value, anchor in a market, craft the message and translate it to execution, with a template or checklist for each step. An optional focus phase returns one step only, and your sector adds that sector's buyer roles, measures and proof points.

sector.description: Your sector in your own words (for example logistics tech, fintech, SaaS, vertical SaaS, AI native, IT services, telecom, software or cybersecurity). Adds how the six steps read in that sector. The same as your selected sector; your selected sector wins when both are given

your_sector.description: Your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: IMPACT Framework Guide

tools.name: impact_identify_champions
tools.description: Takes what your product does and the problem it solves, and returns hypotheses for who buys it: the champion, the economic buyer, the technical influencer, commercial and control reviewers and daily users, with warning signs of an anti-champion, a path to develop the champion and what to give them. Optional company name, target company type, price point and sector fit the roles to your market. These are roles to test, not named people.

target_company_type.description: Type of companies you target (e.g., "mid-size fintech companies", "enterprise manufacturers")

price_point.description: What you charge, with the period, in your own words (for example "$50,000 a year" or "$3,750 per month")

your_sector.description: Your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Identify Champions

tools.name: impact_map_alternatives
tools.description: Takes your product and its category, and returns a map of the alternatives your buyers weigh: one card for each competitor you name, the status-quo options you list and doing nothing, where you can lead, and discovery questions to learn more. Optional competitor weaknesses and your strengths fill the cards, and your sector adds its questions and objections. It uses only what you give and says what would sharpen the map.

category.description: Your product category (e.g., "cloud security monitoring", "last-mile delivery software")

competitors.description: List of competitor names, and the status-quo options your buyers use (for example "spreadsheets"). A description in brackets after a name is kept

competitor_weaknesses.description: Known competitor weaknesses or customer complaints, one per line or separated by semicolons. A weakness that names a competitor is shown on its card

your_strengths.description: What you do better than competitors, one per line or separated by semicolons

your_sector.description: Your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Map Alternatives

tools.name: impact_pinpoint_value
tools.description: Takes your target customer, the main outcome they get and what you do that others do not, and returns value proposition statements in three versions, a value matrix for your own figures, proof points ranked from customer results to social proof, versions for different audiences and channels, and questions to test the value. Optional product name, category, customer results and business model shape it.

target_customer.description: Who you serve (e.g., "cloud security leads at mid-size fintech companies")

unique_capability.description: What you do that others cannot/don't

customer_metrics.description: Any customer results data (e.g., "critical exposures down 70% in one quarter; audit preparation from 3 weeks to 4 days")

business_model.description: How you sell (saas, services, connectivity, transactions, marketplace, hardware_software or investment). Used to choose proof types; read from your inputs when not given

your_sector.description: Your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Pinpoint Value

tools.name: impact_anchor_market
tools.description: Takes what your product does and the segments you are weighing, and returns a beachhead market choice: your segments ranked from your own customers, pain and deal size when you give all three (the answer says which method it used), otherwise scored on keywords in their names; a TAM/SAM/SOM calculation that uses only the company counts, deal size and percentages you give; a three-year expansion path and an ICP hypothesis for the chosen segment. It never chooses a segment you did not name: without segments it recommends none and explains how to find yours from your own customers.

potential_segments.description: The market segments you are weighing, in your own words (for example Mid-market fintech, Enterprise banks, Small retail chains). Needed for a recommendation: without segments no segment is chosen, and the answer explains how to find yours

current_customers.description: Description of your current/best customers. With customer pain and average deal size it ranks the segments (the answer says which method it used); without them it is shown only and the keyword presets score the segments

customer_pain.description: The problem your best customers describe, in their words. With current customers and average deal size it ranks the segments from your own inputs; without them the keyword presets are used

average_deal_size.description: Your annual contract value (ACV) as one amount (e.g., "$50,000", "$50K" or "$1.5M"); a range is refused

sales_cycle.description: Typical sales cycle length. Shown in the output; not used in the scoring

company_counts.description: How many companies you could sell to in each segment, one per line or separated by semicolons (for example "Mid-market fintech: 3,200; Enterprise banks: 600"). A single number is read as the count for the recommended segment. Needed for market sizing

percent_matching_icp.description: The percent of those companies that match your ideal customer profile (for example 25). Needed for SAM

year_one_share_percent.description: The share of the matching companies you expect to win in year one, in percent (for example 1). Needed for SOM

your_sector.description: Your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Anchor Market

tools.name: impact_craft_message
tools.description: Takes your target customer, the key benefit and what sets you apart, and returns a positioning statement (full and one sentence), a message hierarchy from tagline to three supporting pillars, versions for different audiences, objection handling and ways to test the message. Optional product name, customer need, category, main competitor and business model fit it to your market. It writes from your own words, in whole sentences.

customer_need.description: The need they have, written as an action (for example "lose days chasing low-risk cloud alerts")

product_category.description: Your product category, written as a noun phrase (for example "cloud security monitoring platform")

business_model.description: How you sell (saas, services, connectivity, transactions, marketplace, hardware_software or investment). Used to choose the cost and proof lines; read from your inputs when not given

your_sector.description: Your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Craft Message

tools.name: impact_translate_execution
tools.description: Takes a positioning statement, your target customer and the key benefit, and returns copy to edit for the channels you choose: a website hero, a LinkedIn tagline and post drafts, a three-email cold sequence, a sales deck outline and a 15-minute demo script, with calls to action that fit your business model and the order to work the channels in. Optional channels, product name and business model shape it.

key_benefit.description: Primary benefit, written as an action (for example "fix critical exposures first")

channels.description: Which channels to cover, from website, linkedin, cold_email, sales_deck and product_demo. Others are listed as not covered; with none, all five are covered

business_model.description: How you sell (saas, services, connectivity, transactions, marketplace, hardware_software or investment). Used to choose calls to action and commercial terms; read from your inputs when not given

your_sector.description: Your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: Translate Execution

tools.name: impact_full_audit
tools.description: Use for a full positioning review or when someone asks help me explain why we are different. Ask what the product does, who it serves and the problem it solves before calling; never invent these or fill missing facts with placeholders such as Not supplied. Clarify what unlabelled numbers mean. For a request only to phrase a message, impact_craft_message also fits; use this tool for the full review. Returns input completeness scores, supplied proof, a positioning draft and next actions. Scores measure how complete the inputs are, not how strong the positioning is. Never invent proof.

product_description.description: What the product or service does, in the user's words. Ask if missing; do not invent or use a placeholder.

target_customer.description: Who it serves, as supplied by the user. Ask if missing. Keep staff ranges as ranges and clarify unlabelled numbers.

problem_solved.description: The problem the user says they solve. Ask if missing; do not invent or use a placeholder.

key_differentiation.description: A difference the user can describe. Leave out if unknown; do not invent uniqueness or proof.

current_positioning.description: Your current positioning statement or tagline

customer_feedback.description: Customer feedback actually supplied by the user. Leave out if absent; never invent quotes or outcomes.

business_model.description: How you sell (saas, services, connectivity, transactions, marketplace, hardware_software or investment). Used in the plan; read from your inputs when not given. It does not change the score

your_sector.description: Your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

tools.title: IMPACT Full Audit
